sources.note: Triggers a safety intervention in image diffusion from the intermediate clean-image estimate rather than from the prompt, and spends optimization only from the first timestep where a violation actually appears — so extra test-time compute is incurred on unsafe inputs and benign latency stays flat as the budget grows.
sources.title: Test-Time Scaling for Safe Text-Guided Image Generation via Intermediate Clean Estimates

sources.note: Shows that the part of a steering vector which breaks a model's refusal behaviour is a separate direction from the part that produces the intended behavioural effect, and learns that direction by constrained optimization so it can be ablated without losing the steering.
sources.title: Safety Cost of Steering Vectors Is Separable and Reducible

sources.note: Builds safety-alignment training data by first having an agent jailbreak a strong teacher and only then asking that teacher to explain why the successful attack worked, so the student is supervised on the mechanism of the attack rather than on the refusal.
sources.title: Dual-Adversarial Safety Alignment: Cultivating Intrinsic Threat Comprehension in LRMs

sources.note: An inference-time safeguard that reads a reasoning model's attention to find key points in its reasoning path and injects safety reflections there, then scales sampling to pick a safe path.
sources.title: ReasoningGuard: Safeguarding Large Reasoning Models with Inference-time Safety Aha Moments

sources.note: Identifies a multimodal failure where models see the risky visual cue but let narrative coherence override safety as reasoning proceeds, and defends against it by extracting intent before generation.
sources.title: Mitigating Safety Context Amnesia in Multimodal Reasoning Models via Intent-Guided Safety Reasoning

sources.note: Automates the hijacking of a reasoning model's own safety reasoning by using a weaker, less-aligned model to simulate execution reasoning and refining attacks from patterns leaked in refusals.
sources.title: AutoRAN: Automated Hijacking of Safety Reasoning in Large Reasoning Models

result.definition: A prompt that induces a model to produce output its alignment training was meant to prevent, and across 6 sources studied here mainly through what defences transfer. The archive's clearest result is that pattern-keyed alignment does not: a model trained on refusals learns which inputs look dangerous rather than what makes them dangerous, and one defence leaves gradient-optimised suffix attacks at 29.50 percent against a base rate of 29.75 -- no effect at all -- while defences supervised on the mechanism of an attack reach 1.25. The two ablations that carry that argument are worth keeping: seeds that actually defeated the teacher are worth about 14.2 points over raw harmful prompts with everything else fixed, and pairing the same successful jailbreaks with a refusal rather than an analysis moves average attack success by 4 points against the analysis's 60. Two cautions. Evaluation is judge-mediated throughout, with one paper's own audit finding two judges disagreeing on 42 percent of the class that determines the score. And a defence that reduces success without closing it should be read as raising cost -- one agentic attack still reaches 18.00 percent while needing nearly twice as many turns.
